title: Drone hyperlapse
summary: A moving time-lapse shot from the air.

blocks.note: 10 s at 25 fps ≈ 250 frames ≈ 8–9 min of flight.

steps: Check the weather, wind and local drone rules before you fly.
Pick a subject with movement: clouds, traffic, water or shadows.
Plan a slow, simple path: straight line, orbit or pan.
Set exposure and white balance manually so frames match.
Use the drone's **hyperlapse mode** if it has one; otherwise fly slowly while shooting at an interval.
Keep enough battery to return home with margin.

items: Slower and longer looks smoother than fast and short.
Shoot just after sunset when lights come on.

steps: Run the pre-flight checks (Manuals › DJI LITO X1). In DJI Fly, set Max Altitude, Max Distance and Auto RTH Altitude to suit local rules.
Flip the remote's flight mode switch to **C (Cine)** for the slowest, smoothest movement.
Gimbal to **Follow** mode in DJI Fly › Settings › Control, so the horizon stays level.
Take off, fly to the start point and frame the shot.
Tap the **Shooting Modes** icon in the camera view and choose **Hyperlapse**. Pick the Hyperlapse type and set its parameters.
Press the **shutter/record** button to start. The drone shoots and compiles the clip itself.
To stop early, tap the stop icon or press the remote's **Flight Pause/Stop** button. The drone hovers.
dji-lito-x1.note: The LITO X1 manual doesn't list the Hyperlapse types; DJI Fly shows them. Don't fly in rain, snow or strong wind.
